title: The Skyline Problem
statement:
A city's skyline is the outer contour of the silhouette formed by all buildings when viewed from a distance.

Given a list of buildings, each described as [left, right, height], compute the skyline.

The skyline is a list of key points [x, height] where the height changes. The last point always has height 0.

Print each key point as "x h" on its own line.
inputFormat:
The first line contains N.
The next N lines each contain three integers: left right height.
outputFormat: Each skyline key point as "x h" on its own line.

examples.explanation: Single building: rises at x=1, drops to 0 at x=5.
